voyage.name: Grote Markt
voyage.content: The market square is the heart of the old town. It covers an area of 1 ha, and on its southern edge is the city belfry (Halletoren/Belfort), which is one of the city's best known landmarks. There are nice views from the tower (see Do below)

voyage.name: Groeninge Museum
voyage.price: 15 EUR / 7 EUR (audioguide and ticket to Arents House and Forum+ included in the entrance)
voyage.content: Known as 'The city museum of Fine Arts', it houses a collection of artworks that span several centuries (14th-20th), focusing mainly on works by painters who lived and worked in Bruges.

voyage.name: Basilica of the Holy Blood (Heilige Bloed Basiliek)
voyage.content: A beautiful church on the Burg square. It houses a relic: a vial of blood that is said to be that of Jesus - and was built in the Gothic style. Try to get there early so you can view the chapel when it is quiet and not filled with tourists. And don't forget to visit the chapel underneath, in heavy Romanesque style - a contrast to the lovely light Gothic above.

voyage.name: Brewery De Halve Maan
voyage.content: This brewery is the only remaining that's still brewing beer inside the city walls. It's also a beer museum and offers a tour of the beer making process. A history of the brewery is provided, as well as an overview of the city from its tower. The tour lasts for 45 min and is a good way to get a feel for Belgian beer making. The tours start at the exact turn of the hour, be at least 15 minutes early as there is a maxi

voyage.name: 2-be Beer Wall and Bar
voyage.content: On the court of a former major's house, "all Belgian beers" are exposed permanently. At the back of the wall, it's also possible to drink a lot of those beers.

voyage.name: Onze Lieve Vrouwkerk
voyage.content: A fascinating church with architecture from the Romanesque and Gothic periods. In the east end of the church are very fine tombs of Charles the Bold and his daughter Mary of Burgundy, in contrasting Gothic and Renaissance styles, despite their superficial similarity. The church also houses one of the few Michelangelo sculptures outside of Italy, the "Madonna with child". To see the "Madonna with Child" an entrance fe

voyage.name: Simbolik - Open Studio and Expo of Nathalie Beelprez
voyage.content: A house, an open studio where thoughts and ideas are born, a place where Beelprez can mix these thoughts and feelings in a symbolic language of forms, her soul, her calligraphy, her world, her language. While she works in her studio, her expo is open for anyone who wants to let time go, read forms and see letters. An open immersion in texts and forms that excite your senses. Selection of handmade letterwork, wall obj

voyage.name: Jerusalem church
voyage.content: In a quiet area of the city, a highly unusual church with octagonal tower built by the Adornes brothers, merchants of Italian extraction. It includes a fine black Tournai marble tomb, late Gothic stained glass, and a tiny and rather spooky chapel containing an effigy of the dead Christ. The entrance fee also covers the Lace Museum in the former Adornes mansion, where you can see local women and girls learning this tr

voyage.name: The Beguinage (Begijnhof)
voyage.content: In the history, many women couldn't find a man, as men were more likely to die in accidents or in a war. Those women could "marry God" and become a beguine. The beguinage, also known as the convent, offered protection for those single ladies. It lies between the centre of the city and the station, with white painted small houses and fine plane trees, is a quiet place to walk; groups are discouraged.

voyage.name: The Hospital of St John
voyage.content: Sint-Janshospitaal contains a museum of six paintings by Hans Memling, within the early medieval hospital buildings.

voyage.name: Choco-Story Museum
voyage.content: This museum is a must-see for chocolate enthusiasts as it describes chocolate's transition from cocoa into chocolate. Its low-cost tasty exhibits make it well worth the time (and Belcolade's gently overt marketing). Be sure to stay for the chocolate making exhibition to get some excellent samplers. Recommend buying tickets online ahead of time. On a Sunday in October 2022 they didn't have room for walk ins, you neede

voyage.name: Diamond Museum
voyage.content: Diamond museum has a large range of exhibits ranging from mining all the way to polishing and all the history in between. Everyday at 12:15 there is a live polishing demonstration.

voyage.name: Lucifernum
voyage.content: An amazing (private) art gallery with a Gothic cemetery in a subtropical garden located in the old Freemasons temple (1756-1882). 1,000 m² of art and mystery in Bruges' old city centre.

voyage.name: Kruispoort
voyage.content: Part of the second city ramparts of 1297. The current gate dates back to the beginning of the 15th century.

voyage.name: Smedenpoort
voyage.content: The first gate was built in 1297-1299 but was rebuilt in 1376-1378. After that there were several changes to the building. The gate is completely surrounded by water. A renovation in 2009 made the gate look shining again.

voyage.name: Ezelpoort
voyage.content: Just like the Smedenpoort, this gate is completely surrounded by water. Nowadays the gate is only used by pedestrians and cyclists. The gate previously also was called the Oostendsche Poort (Ostend Gate) since the road through the gate lead to Ostend.

voyage.name: Gentpoort
voyage.content: One of the four remaining city gates of the second city ramparts of 1297. In the gate building is housed a museum.

voyage.name: Grote Markt and Belfry Climb
voyage.price: 16 EUR for adults 26+; discounts for children & youth.
voyage.content: Climb the 366 steps to the top of the 83-m-high tower. Excellent views of the city, Grote Markt and hear the bells ring up close.

voyage.name: Canal Tour
voyage.price: 15 EUR plus almost obligatory tip to the driver/guide
voyage.content: To see Bruges from another perspective, take a ride on one of the tour boats around the canals — the multilingual guides provide a potted history of the city in just a few minutes — at only a few euros, it's the best introduction to Bruges. A boat tour will show you places which are otherwise unreachable, as not every canal runs next to a street. Advisable to get there at opening time to avoid the crowds. Cannot be r

voyage.name: Horse drawn carts
voyage.content: Carriages can be hired for a romantic 30-minute trip around the old city of Bruges. Carts can carry up to 5 passengers.

voyage.name: Ambassadors Tours Bruges
voyage.content: Passionate local storytellers offer tours in the medieval city center. No old-fashioned tour focussing solely on historical details, but engaging stories to bring the history to life. Reservations advised. Tell Me Stories About Bruges, daily at 10:00, 11:00, 14:00 & 17:00, operated in English. Bruges at Night: Murder, Mystery & Dark Stories, selected days at 18:00 or 20:00.

voyage.name: Bruges Ballooning
voyage.content: Daily hot air balloon flights over the historic centre and its surroundings. The best way to enjoy the romance of Bruges, and its stunning views, from a few hundred metres up in a balloon basket.

voyage.name: Cycle
voyage.price: 8 EUR for 4 hr at most places, 12 EUR for the day
voyage.content: There are many rental shops near the main square, shop around for the best prices. You can also rent right at the train station and get to the city centre quickly; remember to return them by 19:30. Cycle 5 km to Damme, a picturesque village on the river with a windmill and excellent pancakes, and optionally follow on to the coast (another 15 km).

voyage.name: Running
voyage.content: If you are a runner, try running the 7-km circle around the old centre. Walk along the canal and see all of the medieval gates that used to control the traffic in and out of Bruges. Simply stunning!

voyage.name: Jan Breydel stadium
voyage.content: The city has two teams playing soccer in First Division A, the Belgian top tier: Club Brugge KV and Cercle Brugge KSV. They share the Jan Breydel stadium, capacity 29,000, in Sint-Andries district 2 km west of the centre.

voyage.name: Stef's
voyage.content: A fairly cheap option.

voyage.name: Chocolatier Van Oost
voyage.content: If you are willing to spend a little more, Chocolatier Van Oost on Wollestraat is a must for high-quality artisanal chocolate.

voyage.name: Dumon
voyage.content: Excellent, very high-end chocolate creations. They also make chocolate drinks.

voyage.name: Het Chocoladehuisje
voyage.content: Artisan chocolates. Place where you can buy the original chocolate breasts. Has a nice piece in their window on special occasions.

voyage.name: The Chocolate Line
voyage.content: Almost always has original and funny chocolate-art in their window. Run by a (locally) famous chocolatier, Dominique Persoone. Fame comes with a price: The Chocolate Line is quite expensive compared to the many other chocolate stores in Bruges.

voyage.name: Rombaux
voyage.content: A record, guitar and piano store, run by a friendly family in a landmark building, incredible atmosphere with a huge collection of jazz, classical but also modern records. They further have a guitar and piano instrument department and a good collection of sheet music.

voyage.name: Books & Brunch
voyage.content: An ideal combo of second hand book store and a brunch/dessert-eatery (but you can just have a cup of coffee or a tea too).

voyage.name: The Olive Street Food
voyage.price: €8.9 for a medium-sized wrap, €14.9 for a larger box of food (May 2025)
voyage.content: An authentic Greek takeaway place just a minute of walking away from the Belfry/Grote Markt. They offer food that is not only well-seasoned and extraordinarily savoury, but also very affordable, especially compared to other places to eat at in the Bruges' historical centre.

voyage.name: Brasserie Medard
voyage.content: Huge deal for low budget just near the centre: a mountain of (tasty) spaghetti with tomato sauce, cheese, and mushrooms for 3 EUR. Two options on the menu: vegetarian, non-vegetarian - both at the same price. Double its size for just 2 EUR extra. Very cheap beer too (kriek at 1.50 EUR) (all prices as of July 2010). Most tables order the spaghetti. Tourists aren't welcome until they sit: be sure to sit down and impose

voyage.name: Le Pain Quotidien
voyage.content: A sandwich chain founded in Brussels but now found in the US, France and a number of other countries. Most of the food is organic, and the sandwiches (in particular the Tartine Bouef Basilic) are delicious. Somewhat expensive.

voyage.name: The Potato Bar
voyage.price: €3-4.5 for fries with toppings, €8-11 for a burger (Sept 2021)
voyage.content: One of the better fries shops (frietkoten/frituren) Bruges has to offer. Both classic fries with mayonnaise as well as burgers and fries with a variety of toppings available. Vegetarian options.

voyage.name: Cropains
voyage.price: €6-€8 for a grilled sandwich or wrap
voyage.content: Not much indoor seating, but delicious "croque monsieurs" (grilled sandwiches) and wraps, with vegetarian options.

voyage.name: Brasserie Forestière
voyage.content: Nice and calm restaurant, good food, not too expensive. Good menu for vegetarians. Meal of the day (soup, main dish, dessert or coffee/tea) costs 14 EUR (May 2019) although this is the cheapest menu it has little choice.

voyage.name: Bistrobar Boreas
voyage.content: Fish of the Day, Grilled chicken fillet, Vegan Portobello, Rumpsteak, etc.

voyage.name: L'Estaminet
voyage.content: Good food, nice terrace, cool bartender. Try the renowned spaghetti for 13 EUR, or the delicious croque monsieur for 10 EUR.

voyage.name: De Bottelier
voyage.content: A favourite restaurant of many of Bruges' residents. Very reasonable prices and excellent food. Closed Sunday and Monday nights.

voyage.name: Tom's Diner
voyage.content: Fantastic upmarket take on satisfying, home cooked food. Prices are reasonable, as well.

voyage.name: Petite Aneth
voyage.content: With only 7 tables, small and cosy, with a personal touch.

voyage.name: Cambrinus
voyage.content: This is a very popular place, and for a reason. They have some of the best selection of Belgian beers, more than 440 in total. Some beers have really odd names like Satan, Lucifer, Nostradamus, or the Brunette. It's primarily a restaurant though, as all their hearty food are prepared with a special kind of beer. It's really delicious. Mains go for 17-19 EUR, but they also have the 26 EUR prix fixe "Menu van de Brouwe

voyage.name: Grand Cafe Passage
voyage.content: Attached to the Passage hotel/hostel (see below) is the atmospheric Grand Café, serving traditional Belgian cuisine and beers. Prices are slightly lower than the tourist traps and well worth it. Try the beef stew (very tender) or the ribs.

voyage.name: Trattoria Trium
voyage.content: This is a great spot to have a nice dish of pasta or pizza and is fully Italian. They also sell olive oil, pasta sauces and other authentic products. The decor has a warm home feeling. Try out their antipasto and the excellent house wine. 15-20 EUR.

voyage.name: Curiosa
voyage.content: A good place for a lunch and a beer.

voyage.name: Maximiliaan van Oostenrijk
voyage.content: Midrange restaurant offering plenty to eat including oysters and meat cooked several ways plus, of course, frites. There is not much for vegetarians.

voyage.name: In 't Nieuw Museum
voyage.content: Belgian grill restaurant, well off the tourist track. Excellent steaks, reasonable prices.

voyage.name: Kok au Vin
voyage.content: Memorable Kok au Vin (both the appetiser and the restaurant); the prices are reasonable for the high quality. Family owned and run. Reservations recommended.

voyage.name: Den Gouden Harynck
voyage.content: Gastronomic restaurant which offers three course meals.

voyage.name: De Garre
voyage.content: Hidden in a backyard, this pub offers a nice atmosphere and about 100 kinds of beer, including localy-brewed ones. The house beer is called 'Triple de Garre' and is 11% strong, a good way to start the night. The pub is very often full, but there's a limit of two drinks per person, which means that new places become available pretty quickly.

voyage.name: 't Brugs Beertje
voyage.content: This excellent pub (recommended in the CAMRA guide to the Benelux region) has hundreds of different beers and an authentic beer-cafe atmosphere. Clientele is majority tourists. The front bar is crowded; what looks like the door through to the restrooms opens on another bar area. In 2005 it was closed for most of July - this might be an annual occurrence.

voyage.name: Café Vlissinghe
voyage.content: One of the less touristy bars, with a nice selection of draught and bottled beers. It's probably the oldest pub in Bruges dating from 1515.

voyage.name: Bruges Beer Festival
voyage.content: Annual beer festival held over two days in the Bruges Meeting & Convention Centre. Over 50 breweries represented. Unlike many other beer festivals, this one is not at a fixed time during the year. (see website)

voyage.name: Camping Memling
voyage.content: The only camping-site in Bruges, 3.2 km from the Markt.

voyage.name: Lybeer Travellers' Hostel
voyage.content: In the city centre. Has a mixture of private rooms and dorms. Good common area and bar. Pub crawls and beer tasting are available.

voyage.name: Passage
voyage.content: Very clean and quiet, centrally located Hotel/Hostel with a restaurant-bar downstairs. The name "Passage" comes from the little alley-way right next to the building which you have to pass through in order to reach the reception. Prices for the hostel are around 14 EUR and breakfast costs an extra 5 EUR.

voyage.name: Snuffel Backpacker Hostel
voyage.content: Friendly, a straight line from the central Markt and cheap. Breakfast is included and cheap internet available, with free Wi-Fi. And the bunk beds have ladders. Live music on regular basis, in the bar with the cheapest beers in town where tourists and locals get together!

voyage.name: St Christopher’s @ The Bauhaus Hostel
voyage.content: Part of the St. Christopher's Inn hostel chain. Beds include locker, privacy curtain, reading lights and individual power-points.

voyage.name: ibis budget Brugge Centrum Station
voyage.content: An economical choice from this well known chain right next to the railway station.

voyage.name: Atlas Guesthouse
voyage.price: From 85 EUR per night for a double room
voyage.content: Located between the forest and the historic city of Bruges, this cottage offers spacious accommodation with modern facilities including free Wi-Fi. Atlas Guesthouse has bicycles available to rent and a large terrace with a barbecue. Flat-screen cable TV with a DVD player is provided in the living room which includes a large sofa. The cottage features a kitchen with a hob and an oven. Atlas Guesthouse also has a washi

voyage.name: Hotel Acacia
voyage.price: From 98 EUR per night for a double room
voyage.content: Ideal location behind the Market Square and Belfry (car free area) situated between the two main shopping streets of Bruges. Free wifi, a cosy lounge and terrace. Must see the parrot Coco who greets the guests every day!

voyage.name: Asinello B&B
voyage.content: Lovely bed & breakfast with 3 private rooms, each with their own bathroom. A hammam is also onsite. This is a great option for a romantic weekend.

voyage.name: De Notelaar
voyage.content: Bed and breakfast outside of the city centre.

voyage.name: Eleven B&B
voyage.content: They can host up to 11 people, ideal for families, ask to cook you their lobster meal.

voyage.name: Hotel De Tuilerieën
voyage.content: Famous hotel.

voyage.name: Hotel de Goezeput
voyage.content: Modern and comfortable rooms in a traditional building. Relatively close to the station.

voyage.name: Hotel 't Keizershof
voyage.content: On a quiet street near the station, has rooms starting at 50 EUR and is not far from the centre. Basic breakfast is available.

voyage.name: Hotel Salvators
voyage.price: From 70 EUR per night for a double room
voyage.content: Quirky art hotel in the centre, next to St Salvators Church. This traditional Bruges townhouse has been thoughtfully renovated, with each of the rooms decorated in its own style. Some of the rooms have en-suite jacuzzi, and some sleep up to 5 people. The hotel offers internet access and cycle hire for guests.

voyage.name: Hotel Asiris
voyage.content: A restored patrician residence in the shadow of the 15th century St-Gillis church, with 13 rooms, 75 EUR for a double room. You can also reserve a parking place for 15 EUR / night.

voyage.name: Hotel 't Voermanshuys
voyage.price: 60 EUR for a double with shared toilet/shower
voyage.content: Clean, spacious rooms in the centre. Very friendly staff and includes a substantial breakfast.

voyage.name: Hotel Prinsenhof
voyage.content: This elegant and friendly four star hotel is perfectly situated near the Grand Place & historic town centre of Bruges, with secure private parking.

voyage.name: Hotel Bliss
voyage.content: Small hotel with 19 rooms, situated in centre. It is easily reached via the E40 (exit8) and you will find the hotel right opposite the main exit of the underground car-park.

voyage.name: Hotel Floris Karos
voyage.content: 3 star hotel a few minutes away from market square.

voyage.name: NH Hotel Brugge
voyage.content: Good food and comfortable beds near to parking on the inner ring road, the concert hall and main bus station, in an attractive and completely modernised old building. The staff are obliging and helpful and food is excellent at all meals. Salads, main courses and desserts were all a delight, with the desserts scoring particularly high for attractive presentation. If there was a weak spot, it was the quality of the ora

voyage.name: Hotel Monsieur Maurice
voyage.content: Within the oldest ramparts of the medieval city, in the heart of the city, but in the middle of a green area.

voyage.name: Ibis Brugge Centrum
voyage.content: This chain hotel is conveniently located and comfortable.

voyage.name: Boniface Hotel
voyage.content: The charm of a private home and the comfort of a deluxe hotel.

voyage.name: Hotel The Pand
voyage.content: Located in an 18th-century building.

voyage.name: Canalside House
voyage.content: Built in the 17th century as a gracious townhouse, it now provides the guests two luxurious suites with unrivalled panoramic view of the canal and the imposing church of Our Lady's.

voyage.name: Novotel Brugge
voyage.content: The Novotel forms a complex with the Ibis, cleverly hidden within the very heart of the old town of Brugge, and offering the usual Novotel family-friendly facilities, including even a small outdoor pool.

voyage.name: Crowne Plaza Brugge
voyage.content: A regular Crowne Plaza with some top-level rooms under sloping wooden roofs.
